title: Portal Paddle events and the sales ledger
description: The spec's two sentences kept apart: every Paddle event stored exactly as received, and a readable sales ledger derived from it (portal plan P4.2, F16). The event is Paddle's and is never edited — it is the record of a sale counsel's retention item is about (D457) — and the entry is the portal's reading of it, so a figure in a report can always be walked back to the body it came from. An event is stored before it is processed, which is why it carries a state of its own: a retry that arrives while the first delivery is still being read finds it already there. Every object here is closed, because ee/keyservice/wire_ledger.go decodes it with DisallowUnknownFields.

event.description: One Paddle notification as it arrived, stored before anything was made of it.

id.description: Paddle's event id, and the digest of the body for one that does not decode: an undecodable body is stored too, and it has no id of Paddle's to be stored under. The id is what makes a redelivery idempotent (F16).

received_at.description: When the delivery was received, in UTC. It is this service's clock and not the body's: what the body says about when it was sent is a claim inside a body, and the window the signature is checked in is read from the signed header (F16).

signature.description: The signature header the delivery carried, kept beside the body because it is what proved the body was Paddle's. A delivery whose signature was not verified never reaches this shape: verification is first, and an unverified body is never stored (P4.2's TestUnverifiedBodyIsNeverStored).

notification.description: Paddle's own name for the event, as the body spells it, and empty for a body that was stored without decoding. It is Paddle's word and not the ledger's: an entry's kind is the portal's (see `entry`).

body.description: The verified body exactly as received, as text. Text is the one form that holds a body that decodes and one that does not, and "exactly as received" is the whole point: the signature was over these bytes.

state.description: What the portal has made of the event. Stored is a body that arrived and has not been read yet; undecodable is one answered 400 so Paddle retries; processed is one a ledger entry exists for; parked is one whose transaction and subscription did not begin with a transaction this API created, waiting for operations (F15, P5.1); dismissed is operations ending one. The stored body is never edited by any of them.

entitlement_id.description: What a processed or attached event resolved to, or null while it resolved to nothing — a parked event has no entitlement until operations attaches it (P5.1).

entry.description: One line of the readable sales ledger, derived from one stored event.

id.description: The stored event's id: an entry is what one event was read as, so one event makes one line, and a refund is an event of its own rather than an edit of the purchase.

at.description: When the money moved, in UTC — the event's own instant and not the instant it was received, which is what a month's report is bounded by (P5.2's TestReportMonthsAreUTC).

kind.description: What the event did to the money, in the portal's words: Paddle's notification names are a provider's vocabulary and not a ledger's.

organisation_id.description: The organisation the money was for, resolved from the transaction the API created (F15).

workspace_id.description: The portal workspace the money was for, or null for a line whose event named none.

entitlement_id.description: The entitlement the purchase created or the refund resolved to, or null for a line that resolved to none. A purchase creates an entitlement and never a key (D2196).

amount_micros.description: The amount in micro-dollars, signed: a refund is the negative of what it gives back, and the reports add these up. Micro-dollars are the unit the rest of this repository counts money in, so no arithmetic here is done in a float.

currency.description: The currency the amount is in, as an ISO 4217 code. It is kept per line because Paddle prices a currency and not this service.

seats.description: How many seats the line covers, so a report can say what was bought and not only what it cost.

channel.description: Whether the sale was direct or through a reseller: the split the reports are asked for (spec §Operations, D2190). It is on the line because the reseller link can change afterwards (operations can relink a customer, P6.1), and a report of March must read March's channel.
